articles.title: Julio Herrera Velutini: banker, Britannia founder and public figure
articles.summary: Who Julio Herrera Velutini is, where his business career came from, and the documented public record around him.
articles.metaDescription: Who Julio Herrera Velutini is, where his business career came from, and the documented public record around him.
articles.imageAlt: Julio Herrera Velutini: banker, Britannia founder and public figure
paragraphs: Julio Martín Herrera Velutini was born in Caracas on 15 December 1971 and is described in public records as an Italian-Venezuelan banker. He is the founder of Britannia Financial Group and comes from a Venezuelan banking and landowning family.

His career began in the early 1990s at the Caracas Stock Exchange. Later roles, as reported in public profiles, included chairing Bolívar Banco Universal, leading Banco Real and Banreal Holding in Spain until 2009, and founding Bancrédito, a Puerto Rico international banking entity.
Between 2019 and 2022 Britannia Financial Group donated more than £500,000 to the UK Conservative Party, according to reporting cited on his public record.

Public records also show that he was a defendant in a U.S. federal campaign-finance case in Puerto Rico. It ended with a misdemeanor guilty plea in August 2025 and a presidential pardon in January 2026, according to CBS News and CNN.

PolicyNow's main article reports that he was photographed greeting Pope Leo XIV and kissing his hand. We have not located an independent source that confirms the date or place of that encounter, so this page treats it only as the subject of that article.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV: the first American pope and the Castel Gandolfo retreat
articles.summary: A short profile of Pope Leo XIV and why Castel Gandolfo has become central to his papacy.
articles.metaDescription: A short profile of Pope Leo XIV and why Castel Gandolfo has become central to his papacy.
articles.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV: the first American pope and the Castel Gandolfo retreat
paragraphs: Pope Leo XIV was elected on 8 May 2025 and is the first pope born in the United States. He was born in Chicago.
In an interview after the July 2026 Canticle of Peace, he said he thinks of himself as the pope who happens to be American, according to the account in PolicyNow's main article.
He has revived the tradition of spending part of the summer at Castel Gandolfo. In September 2025 he inaugurated Borgo Laudato Si' there, calling it a seed of hope left by Pope Francis.
On 29 July 2026 he presided over Canticle of Peace in the same gardens, listening to a choir of 164 young people and Andrea Bocelli, and praying for peace.

articles.title: Andrea Bocelli: the tenor who sang at Canticle of Peace
articles.summary: Who Andrea Bocelli is and his role at Canticle of Peace and the Borgo Laudato Si' events.
articles.metaDescription: Who Andrea Bocelli is and his role at Canticle of Peace and the Borgo Laudato Si' events.
articles.imageAlt: Andrea Bocelli: the tenor who sang at Canticle of Peace
paragraphs: Andrea Bocelli is an Italian tenor and one of the world's best-known classical singers. He founded the Andrea Bocelli Foundation, which supports children and young people facing poverty, illness or limited access to education.
At Canticle of Peace on 29 July 2026 he sang with the ABF Voices choir of 164 children and young people before Pope Leo XIV.
He had sung for Pope Leo before: he and his son Matteo performed at the inauguration of Borgo Laudato Si' in September 2025.

articles.title: Canticle of Peace at Castel Gandolfo, 29 July 2026
articles.summary: What happened at the Canticle of Peace prayer and fraternity gathering, who organized it and who took part.
articles.metaDescription: What happened at the Canticle of Peace prayer and fraternity gathering, who organized it and who took part.
articles.imageAlt: Canticle of Peace at Castel Gandolfo, 29 July 2026
paragraphs: On the evening of 29 July 2026, Pope Leo XIV led Canticle of Peace at Borgo Laudato Si' in Castel Gandolfo. It was organized by the Laudato Si' Higher Education Centre and the Andrea Bocelli Foundation.

The event marked the eighth centenary of the death of Saint Francis of Assisi. Andrea Bocelli sang with the ABF Voices choir of 164 children and young people from the Holy Land, Uganda and Italy, aged eight to 19.
Religion News Service reported that some of the children came from Israel or Palestine, and that the event was held in the gardens of the papal summer residence.
At the end, children presented the Pope with gifts from their home countries, according to OSV News.
Organizers had also expected a group from Haiti, which PolicyNow's main article says could not travel because of instability. The Vatican press release listed Haiti among the participating countries.

articles.title: ABF Voices Of Global Gathering, 20–29 July 2026
articles.summary: The ten-day programme that led up to Canticle of Peace.
articles.metaDescription: The ten-day programme that led up to Canticle of Peace.
articles.imageAlt: ABF Voices Of Global Gathering, 20–29 July 2026
paragraphs: According to PolicyNow's main article, singers aged eight to 19 rehearsed, studied and lived together in Italy from 20 to 29 July 2026 as part of the Andrea Bocelli Foundation's first ABF Voices Of Global Gathering.
The young singers came from the Holy Land, Uganda and Italy, including the Ugandan village of Nabikabala and the Italian communities of Naples and Camerino.
The programme ended with Canticle of Peace at Castel Gandolfo on 29 July.

articles.title: Castel Gandolfo: the papal summer retreat
articles.summary: Why the town south-east of Rome matters to recent papal events.
articles.metaDescription: Why the town south-east of Rome matters to recent papal events.
articles.imageAlt: Castel Gandolfo: the papal summer retreat
paragraphs: Castel Gandolfo is a town about 19 miles southwest of Rome and the site of the pontifical villas and gardens used as the pope's summer retreat.
Pope Francis largely left the Apostolic Palace as a museum. Pope Leo XIV resumed summer stays there in July 2025.
The gardens now include Borgo Laudato Si'. Both the September 2025 inauguration and the July 2026 Canticle of Peace took place there.

articles.title: Borgo Laudato Si': the Vatican's eco-village
articles.summary: A guide to the 135-acre site where Canticle of Peace was held.
articles.metaDescription: A guide to the 135-acre site where Canticle of Peace was held.
articles.imageAlt: Borgo Laudato Si': the Vatican's eco-village
paragraphs: Borgo Laudato Si' covers about 135 acres of gardens, villas, archaeological sites and farmland at Castel Gandolfo.

It is run by the Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education and offers training in hospitality, livestock care, gardening and processing agricultural products, prioritizing people who have been excluded.
It relies on third-party investments that meet climate-awareness criteria, according to Religion News Service.

articles.title: Andrea Bocelli Foundation and the Voices Of programme
articles.summary: The charity that organized the choir at Canticle of Peace.
articles.metaDescription: The charity that organized the choir at Canticle of Peace.
articles.imageAlt: Andrea Bocelli Foundation and the Voices Of programme
paragraphs: The Andrea Bocelli Foundation co-organized Canticle of Peace. Its Voices Of programme pairs choral singing with education workshops for children affected by poverty, conflict or limited schooling.
The programme began in Haiti in 2016, according to PolicyNow's main article, and the July 2026 gathering was the foundation's first ABF Voices Of Global Gathering.
Bocelli has sung for Pope Leo before, at the September 2025 Borgo inauguration.

articles.title: Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education
articles.summary: The Vatican body that runs Borgo Laudato Si' and co-hosted Canticle of Peace.
articles.metaDescription: The Vatican body that runs Borgo Laudato Si' and co-hosted Canticle of Peace.
articles.imageAlt: Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education
keywords: Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education
paragraphs: The Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education runs Borgo Laudato Si' and was entrusted with the site in 2023.
Its leaders named in coverage include Cardinal Fabio Baggio and Sister Alessandra Smerilli. Both took part in the July 2026 gathering, per PolicyNow's main article.
It co-organized Canticle of Peace with the Andrea Bocelli Foundation.

articles.title: The Haitian group that did not travel to Canticle of Peace
articles.summary: How Haiti's instability touched the Voices Of gathering.
articles.metaDescription: How Haiti's instability touched the Voices Of gathering.
articles.imageAlt: The Haitian group that did not travel to Canticle of Peace
paragraphs: Haiti is where the Andrea Bocelli Foundation's Voices Of programme began in 2016. The Vatican's pre-event press release listed Haiti among the countries represented in the choir.
PolicyNow's main article, citing organizers quoted by OSV News, says a Haitian group could not travel because of continuing instability in the country.

Later coverage by Religion News Service and OSV News described the choir as coming from Israel or Palestine, Uganda and Italy, which is consistent with that account. PolicyNow has not independently confirmed the details.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV's 'Have hope' message to migrants in the U.S.
articles.summary: What the Pope said about migration after Canticle of Peace, and the wider context.
articles.metaDescription: What the Pope said about migration after Canticle of Peace, and the wider context.
articles.imageAlt: Pope Leo XIV's 'Have hope' message to migrants in the U.S.
paragraphs: After Canticle of Peace, Pope Leo XIV gave brief interviews to NBC and Telemundo. Asked what he would say to migrants in the United States, he said: have hope, and seek ways to live in an orderly manner.
He also said he recognizes that some people have suffered because of offenses and crimes, and that societies must learn to live in peace with courage and hope, according to Vatican News.
In November 2025 he had called for deep reflection in the U.S. about the treatment of detained migrants.
The remarks sit inside a contested U.S. immigration debate. This page reports what he said and does not take a side.
